books.section: Massachusetts and the New England Colonies

primary_sources: Roger Williams, The Hireling Ministry None of Christ's (1652)

options.text: Puritans only, and no one else.

options.misconception: Massachusetts did not welcome all Protestants — it banished dissenters like Williams himself.
The Bay Colony protected no Christians but its own — Catholics and Quakers were not welcome.
Williams is arguing for wider freedom, not describing what his critics believed — his critics kept freedom narrow.

rationales.A: Williams attacks a government that imposes one religion — the Massachusetts authorities kept worship for their own Puritan church alone.
rationales.B: Massachusetts did not welcome all Protestants — it banished dissenters like Williams himself.
rationales.C: The Bay Colony protected no Christians but its own — Catholics and Quakers were not welcome.
rationales.D: Williams is arguing for wider freedom, not describing what his critics believed — his critics kept freedom narrow.
rationales.general:
1. Ask who Williams is arguing against. A government that imposes a religion on people's souls.
2. Ask whose religion that government imposed. Massachusetts Bay's — the Puritan church alone.
3. Flip it around. The critics' freedom was freedom for Puritans only.
Remember: to find what a critic's opponents believed, read what the critic attacks — the attack names the belief.

stimulus.source_note: Roger Williams, The Hireling Ministry None of Christ's (1652), verbatim, public domain.
stimulus.text: I observe the great and wonderful mistake, both our own and our fathers, as to the civil powers of this world, acting in spiritual matters. I have read…the last will and testament of the Lord Jesus over many times, and yet I cannot find…that ever He would have put forth the least finger of temporal or civil power in the matters of His spiritual affairs and Kingdom. Hence must it lamentably be against the testimony of Christ Jesus for the civil state to impose upon the souls of the people a religion, a worship, a ministry….
